items.readable_text:
Content:
The pivots of a matrix in row echelon form are the first non-zero entries in each row of the matrix.

Content:
For example, given the matrix
[MATH: [1|0|− 2|0; 0|1|5|0; 0|0|0|1]]
which is in row echelon form, let's find the pivots of [MATH: A.]

Content:
- The first non-zero entry in the first row is the entry [MATH: a_{11}=1.] So this is a pivot.
- The first non-zero entry of the second row is [MATH: a_{22}=1.] So this is also a pivot.
- The first non-zero entry in the third row is [MATH: a_{34}=1.] Therefore this is a pivot.

Content:
The pivots of [MATH: A] are highlighted below.

Content:
[MATH: [1|0|− 2|0; 0|1|5|0; 0|0|0|1]]

Content:
The pivot columns of a matrix in row echelon form are simply the columns in which the pivots appear.

Content:
For our matrix [MATH: A], we can see that the pivot columns are the [MATH: 1]st, [MATH: 2]nd, and [MATH: 4]th columns.

Content:
The non-pivot columns are the columns that do not contain a pivot. So for the matrix [MATH: A,] the only non-pivot column is the [MATH: 3]rd column.

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
The pivots of a matrix in row echelon form are the first non-zero entries in each row of the matrix.

Content:
For example, given the matrix
[MATH: [1|0|− 2|0; 0|1|5|0; 0|0|0|1]]
which is in row echelon form, let's find the pivots of [MATH: A.]

Content:
- The first non-zero entry in the first row is the entry [MATH: a_{11}=1.] So this is a pivot.
- The first non-zero entry of the second row is [MATH: a_{22}=1.] So this is also a pivot.
- The first non-zero entry in the third row is [MATH: a_{34}=1.] Therefore this is a pivot.

Content:
The pivots of [MATH: A] are highlighted below.

Content:
[MATH: [1|0|− 2|0; 0|1|5|0; 0|0|0|1]]

Content:
The pivot columns of a matrix in row echelon form are simply the columns in which the pivots appear.

Content:
For our matrix [MATH: A], we can see that the pivot columns are the [MATH: 1]st, [MATH: 2]nd, and [MATH: 4]th columns.

Content:
The non-pivot columns are the columns that do not contain a pivot. So for the matrix [MATH: A,] the only non-pivot column is the [MATH: 3]rd column.

---
